kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: New book revisits the 2023 killing of an unhoused man in crisis on the NYC subway
wire.summary: Jordan Neely was frightening fellow passengers. A former Marine named Daniel Penny put Neely into a chokehold, killing him. Journalist Anand Giridharadas investigates the incident in Man in the Mirror.

wire.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn
wire.summary: The Federal Reserve opted to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged — but investors widely expect the central bank to raise rates at its next meeting in December to combat stubborn inflation.

wire.title: Dolores Huerta, influential labor leader, feminist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
wire.summary: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread rallying cry.

wire.title: What's gone up even faster than gas or rent? The cost of caregiving
wire.summary: A new study from AARP shows caregivers' out-of-pocket costs rose about 60% in the last five years.

wire.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
wire.summary: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

wire.title: Dozens are dead in a high-speed train crash in Spain
wire.summary: The toll is rising after a high-speed train between slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped south of Madrid, derailing two cars. It was Spain's second major train accident this year.

wire.title: Senate candidates built up massive campaign war chests with out-of-state donations
wire.summary: In several competitive U.S. Senate contests, candidates have built healthy campaign accounts with out-of-state donations. But the messages to those donors is very different from the one back at home.

wire.title: Why many student voters have a right to choose where to register to vote
wire.summary: Student voters studying outside their hometown have a right to choose where they register to vote. Advocates say a Montana legal fight is a reminder of a misunderstanding of those students' rights.

wire.title: Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims
wire.summary: Congressional Democrats are working with good governance groups to create an action plan for any potential claims of election fraud.

wire.title: Are you an organ donor? Here are some rule changes you may want to know
wire.summary: Transplant teams can talk to families about organ donation before they've decided whether to continue life-sustaining medical care for loved ones. Until now, that has been forbidden.

wire.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
wire.summary: With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.

wire.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
wire.summary: With 85% of votes counted, all signs point to an impasse. The most likely outcome may be new elections.

wire.title: Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
wire.summary: The Villa Vie Odyssey suspended its voyage and is working with passengers on "temporary living arrangements".

wire.title: Serbian shot dead after attacking officer outside Israeli embassy, minister says
wire.summary: Authorities say the attacker in Belgrade was an underage male who was being monitored by security services.

wire.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
wire.summary: The energy minister described it as a "major milestone" for the East African nation.

wire.title: Anger in Kenya over extradition hearing delay for ex-British soldier accused of murdering woman
wire.summary: No official reason has been given for postponing next month’s hearing to May 2027, the family says.
